newsitem.title: USA: Wash. board approves Puget Sound merger.
newsitem.headline: Wash. board approves Puget Sound merger.

text.p: Puget Sound Power & Light Co said Wednesday that Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission had approved its planned merger with Washington Energy Co.
The two companies said their boards of directors would meet separately Friday to review the commission's order and vote on the merger.
If both boards approve the new company, Puget Sound Energy, could be formed at the close of New York Stock Exchange trading Monday and begin trading Tuesday under Puget Power's symbol, PSD.
The transportation commission decision ratified a settlement on terms of the merger reached between the two companies and state officials in December.

Under the decision, Puget Power residential electricity customers will see an immediate decrease in rates of 3.24 percent and then increases of no more than 1.5 percent in each of the next four years, the commission said.
Rates for customers of Washington Energy's natural gas subsidiary will remain steady until 1999 then decrease by 1 percent for all customer classes, the commission said.

The commission also approved a service quality program that provides for penalties of up to $7.5 million a year for failing to meet standards and customer payments of $50 for missed service apppointements.
Under the merger agreement, announced in October 1995, each share of Washington Energy will be exchanged for 0.86 share of Puget Sound Power, which was up 1/4 at 25-3/4.
At current levels, that values Washington Energy, which has about 24.3 million shares outstanding, at $538 million.
Puget Power has 860,000 electricity customers in western Washington, while Washington Energy provides natural gas service to 500,000 customers.
The two companies have combined annual revenues of about $1.63 billion and have projected cost savings of $370 million over 10 years.
A company spokesman said 270 employees, or about 8 percent of the work force, have agreed to leave the two companies under a voluntary separation program offered last year.
